Definition.Label: Core Definition
Definition.Title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
Definition.OneLiner: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI architecture that enhances Large Language Models by retrieving relevant factual information from external knowledge bases before generating a response, ensuring grounded, verifiable, and hallucination-free answers.
Definition.Formula: Generated Output = LLM(User Query + Retrieved Context)

KeyBenefits.Label: Zero Fine-Tuning
KeyBenefits.Desc: Connect private data without expensive GPU retraining.

KeyBenefits.Label: Real-Time Freshness
KeyBenefits.Desc: Overcome LLM knowledge cutoff dates instantly.

KeyBenefits.Label: Auditable Citations
KeyBenefits.Desc: Trace every claim back to exact source documents.

Stages.title: Document Ingestion & Parsing
Stages.summary: Extract raw content from enterprise documents (PDF, Markdown, HTML, Notion, APIs) and cleanse boilerplate noise.

details.whatHappens: Raw unstructured files are loaded and stripped of non-informative markup, scripts, and duplicate headers. Documents are enriched with metadata such as source URI, creation date, author, and security tags.
details.proTip: 80% of RAG failure modes happen here: tables and multi-column PDFs easily lose spatial meaning if parsed with basic regex extractors.

Stages.title: Text Chunking & Splitting
Stages.summary: Partitioning long documents into semantically coherent passages with bounded token windows and overlap.

details.whatHappens: Long text is broken down into fixed or adaptive chunks (e.g. 256 to 512 tokens). A 10–20% sliding window overlap ensures boundary ideas are not truncated in isolation.
details.proTip: Use Parent Document Retriever: embed small chunks (128 tokens) for precise search, but return the larger parent chunk (1024 tokens) to the LLM for rich context.

Stages.title: Dense Vector Embeddings
Stages.summary: Converting text chunks into high-dimensional numerical vectors capturing deep conceptual and semantic meaning.

details.whatHappens: Each chunk is transformed by an embedding model into a vector of numbers (e.g. 768 to 3072 floating points). Similar ideas cluster close together in geometric space.
details.proTip: Ensure the embedding model used during document ingestion is identical to the one used for runtime query embedding, and normalize vectors for fast dot-product similarity.

Stages.title: Vector Database & Indexing
Stages.summary: Indexing vectors and metadata using Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms for sub-millisecond retrieval.

details.whatHappens: Vectors are indexed using specialized data structures such as HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) or IVF (Inverted File). Metadata is stored side-by-side to allow pre-filtering.
details.proTip: Always apply metadata filtering (e.g., department, user role, document date) before vector distance scoring to dramatically reduce candidate search space.

Stages.title: User Query & Pre-retrieval
Stages.summary: Incoming user prompt is cleansed, rewritten, decomposed, and transformed into an embedding vector.

details.whatHappens: User questions are rarely written in the formal tone of reference docs. Advanced pre-retrieval systems apply HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) or sub-query decomposition to expand search intent.
details.proTip: A conversational question like 'Does our plan cover braces?' often fails vector matching unless rewritten into 'Dental insurance coverage for orthodontics and braces'.

Stages.title: Hybrid Search & Reranking
Stages.summary: Combining dense semantic retrieval with sparse keyword search, then scoring top candidates with a Cross-Encoder reranker.

details.whatHappens: Dense vectors capture semantic concepts, while BM25 keyword search captures exact product numbers and codes. Candidates are combined via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), then scored by a Cross-Encoder.
details.proTip: Adding a reranker is the single highest-ROI upgrade to Naive RAG. It consistently boosts Top-3 accuracy by 15–30% with minimal latency overhead.

Stages.title: Prompt Augmentation & Context Assembly
Stages.summary: Fusing retrieved reference passages with system guardrails and the original question into an augmented prompt.

details.whatHappens: Top-ranked context passages are wrapped in clean delimiters (<context>...</context>) with citation IDs. Strict prompt instructions command the model to only use the provided context and avoid assumptions.
details.proTip: LLMs suffer from 'Lost in the Middle' attention degradation. Place the most authoritative chunks at the very beginning and very end of your context block.

Stages.title: Grounded LLM Generation
Stages.summary: The LLM synthesizes an accurate, fluent answer grounded exclusively in the provided context, citing sources.

details.whatHappens: The model acts as a reasoning engine over provided evidence rather than reciting memorized parameters. The final output includes bracketed source citations [1], [2] allowing users to verify provenance.
details.proTip: Keep inference temperature low (0.0 to 0.2) for factual RAG and use automated RAG triade metrics (Context Precision, Faithfulness, Answer Relevance) to guard against drift.

Comparison.naive: Linear: Ingest -> Embed -> Top-K Search -> Prompt
Comparison.advanced: Modular: Query Rewriting -> Hybrid BM25/Dense -> Reranking -> Routing

Comparison.naive: Moderate (suffers from keyword mismatch & hallucinated context)
Comparison.advanced: High (Cross-encoder rerankers filter out semantic false-positives)

Comparison.naive: Static vector DB updates; potential collision
Comparison.advanced: Partitioned metadata, time-decay scoring & dynamic routing
Strict chunk-level provenance with sentence-level grounding
